chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: What a ballyhoo was
summary: Explanation of ballyhooing: bands or shows playing on trucks or outside to draw a crowd.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: There was always so much music around the neighborhood. you know. Like, bands would come to town and they would do what you call a ballyhoo. Have you ever heard of a ballyhoo?
I know the word, but I don't know what it meant.
Well, a ballyhoo is this. A band comes to town and they're going to play a dance. Well, that afternoon they would have a flatbed truck, and they would

sit on this truck and drive through the neighborhoods and play. In other words, it was like a sample of what you're going to get that night. That's what it's called; they called it ballyhooing. And then also...ballyhoo is also for like when the minstrel shows come to town or the medicine show -- you come outside and play. That's a ballyhoo. Then you go back inside and do the performance. But anything to create interest, to draw the people, you know -- that was a ballyhoo. [LAUGHS]
They use the word now, but I didn't really know where it started.
Yeah, that's what it meant. In other words, you're drumming up some business!
